outcome.technical: Edited skills/architecture-map/references/schema-introspection.md. The 'project's own Python' recipe now runs `python3 -I -c` and the text explains why: plain `python -c` puts the cwd first on sys.path, so a repo-owned duckdb.py or sqlite3.py would be imported and executed. The example now takes the DuckDB-section temp copy (`"$tmp/app.duckdb"`, passed via sys.argv) instead of hard-coded /tmp/copy.duckdb. The 'No shipped driver' rule (line 12) now says `python3 -I -c`. If the module is not importable under -I, skip and record it, and do not drop -I. Gate: this task adds no test, so there was nothing of its own to run and I ran none; the orchestrator's recorded `node --test` is the evidence. Dependants (tests/skill-discovery-refs.test.mjs, agents/archmap-explorer.md, agents/archmap-synthesizer.md, docs/design.md, SKILL.md, discovery-generic.md, stack-node-backend.md, stack-python-backend.md): all still correct. They refer to the file by basename. I ran grep for 'python -c', 'python3 -c' and 'copy.duckdb' across them, which exited 0, and the only hit was the edited file itself. The file's name, path and headings are unchanged, so basename references and any heading-based checks are unaffected. I did not run the discovery-refs test.
